scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: You type a website name, press enter, and the page appears in about a second. A lot happens in that second.

scenes.name: dns
scenes.text: Computers don't use names, they use numbers called IP addresses. So your browser asks DNS, the internet's phone book, for the website's number.

scenes.name: chain
scenes.text: If it's not already saved nearby, the lookup goes from root servers, to the dot com servers, to the site's own name server, which gives the answer.

scenes.name: connect
scenes.text: Your browser connects to that IP address, and they agree on encryption keys. That's the padlock you see next to the address.

scenes.name: request
scenes.text: The browser asks for the page, and the server sends back HTML, the page's structure.

scenes.name: assets
scenes.text: The HTML lists images, styles and scripts. The browser fetches those too, often from nearby servers called a CDN.

scenes.name: render
scenes.text: Finally, the browser lays everything out and paints the page on your screen. Often in under a second.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Lookup, connect, request, render. A page in a second. Follow for more on how things really work.
